title: R5 | Allegro: original-size towel
description: Preserves the original R1 cloth shape, scale, table and close/lift/carry/hold/place/release operation. The placement hand height increases by 20-25 mm to clear the finite table with the original hand. Original robot hand geometry replaces the cube jaws. Robot roots and joints are prescribed; all cloth vertices remain dynamic, with no pins or attachments. Allegro starts in declared shallow prepared contact at the original towel edge; no approach acquisition claim.

whole_hand_finite_table_audit.method: Separating-axis test of every original collision-shape OBB against finite original table; palm mesh bounded by its own local vertices; both shape margins included.

recipe_metrics.boundary_conditions: Only original robot roots and joints prescribed; every cloth vertex is free; no pins or attachments.
recipe_metrics.qualification: Preserved-scene contact smoke; no actuator-force, full-arm-reach or calibrated-material claim. Outcomes are measured, not assumed.

task_measurements.method: Conservative whole-object shell AABB versus whole original-hand collision AABB, expanded by shape margin; detection gap excluded. Positive distance establishes geometric separation at the sampled state. Zero is inconclusive, not contact.

support_planes.label: unchanged original start and placement table

scope_limits: Sampled separation evidence, not continuous retention or acquisition qualification.
No force, contact membership, interface slip, target-placement tolerance or fidelity pass is inferred.
Support-plane height is a geometric task observable; negative height outside a finite table is not penetration.
Cable bounds are conservative; particle shell bounds use all vertices and their radii.
AABB overlap can hide separation. Absence of a positive bound cannot establish retention.

dat_contact_coverage.scope: Sticky global rigid/full-surface and soft-self row counts across every owned detection, including preparation; excludes per-body adjacency capacities. Self-contact order: vertex-triangle, edge-edge, triangle-vertex.
